newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -T-bond to make inroads on 113-31 top.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -T-bond to make inroads on 113-31 top.

text.p: September T-bond futures have the potential to break their recent high and bound higher, but may see some consolidation first, technical analysts said on Tuesday.
Raynard Cheng, technical analyst at First Chicago in London, said the outlook for T-bonds remained positive as long as support at 113-15 held.
He said the market may head towards Monday's high at 113-31 ahead of resistance at 114-08, the high on continuation charts on February 18.
"The view is the market is going to test the resistance then react off it," said Cheng.
"The intraday outlook is to test support at 113-15 and if that fails to go to 112-15."
Charts show the market hit a daily high of 113-15 on July 3.
By 1000 GMT, September T-bonds were trading at 113-19 in automated trade, 2/32 below the Chicago settlement.
Adrian Sells, director at Crane Investment Analysis in London, saw range trading for Tuesday's session.
"We closed off the highs a little yesterday, so there is every possibility we will track sideways today."
Monday's low of 113-03 would offer initial support to the market, Sells said.
Cheng said below 112-15, the market could test 111-10.
"Potentially it could go to 111-10 which is the 50 percent retracement from the low at 108-17 in May to the overnight high," he said.
But if the contract remained on an upward track, Sells said it could push to the 114-28/30 area. Continuation charts show T-bonds hit daily highs of 114-31 on December 9, and 114-30 on December 10.
Beyond there, 115-17 beckoned, Sells said. The contract struck a low of 115-17 on December 4 before declining through December and January.
December Eurodollar futures were at 94.065 at 0954 GMT in automated trade, up 0.005.
Support lies around Thursday's close of 94.045, Sells said. If that holds, the contract can head for resistance at 94.10, he added.
